proposal.value: Proposition E would: • Rules Regulating Purchasing: Give the City Administrator exclusive authority to propose ordinances that change how the City selects contractors and enters into contracts for goods, services, construction, and grants (Purchasing). The Board and Mayor may not amend the ordinances, but they can: • Approve or reject the ordinances within 60 days, or • If no action is taken within 60 days, the ordinances would be approved. Proposition E does not change the current Board authority for Purchasing ordinances that mainly address wages, workplace health and safety, utilization of local business, or labor agreements. • Board Approval of Various Agreements: Increase the dollar amount requiring Board approval to: • Contracts and leases that bring in $4,500,000 or more in revenue to the City, • Contracts that cost the City $25,000,000 or more. Starting in 2032, the City’s Controller would adjust these dollar amounts every five years for inflation. Proposition E would require Board approval for major amendments to these agreements. • City Administrator’s Term: Increase the City Administrator’s term from five to ten years. • City Administrator’s Authority: The City Administrator would set Purchasing rules and processes for all goods, services, construction, and grants that all City departments must follow, except as limited by other laws. Most departments would now be subject to the City Administrator’s authority regarding technology policies and the disposal of City personal property. These rules would override those departments’ conflicting rules and policies.

way_it_is_now.value: The City Administrator’s Office is responsible for most of the City’s purchasing. However, authority for the City’s purchasing and technology is shared among the City Administrator’s Office, the Board of Supervisors, the Mayor, and some City departments. • Rules Regulating Purchasing: The Board of Supervisors (Board) may adopt ordinances that set the rules about how the City selects contractors and enters into contracts for goods, services, construction, and grants (referred to below as Purchasing). • Board Approval of Various Agreements: With some exceptions, the City’s Charter requires the Board to approve: • Contracts and leases that bring in $1,000,000 or more in revenue to the City, and • Contracts that cost the City $10,000,000 or more. The Board must also approve certain amendments to these agreements. • City Administrator’s Term: The Mayor appoints the City Administrator to a five-year term, subject to Board approval. • City Administrator’s Authority: The City Administrator sets Purchasing rules and processes governing goods and services except for some goods and services of the Municipal Transportation Agency, Public Utilities Commission, Port Commission, and some arts departments. The City Administrator also oversees technology policies and manages disposal of City personal property for most departments.
